page: Hetzner Cloud ccx63 is a dedicated CPU server instance featuring 48 vCPUs and 24 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this virtualized instance utilizes the QEMU hypervisor. It is equipped with 188.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.91 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with a local 960 GB NVMe SSD, while the instance does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and single-core CPU capabilities. The instance achieves top 25% performance in stress-ng CPU tests, PassMark CPU benchmarks, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Cryptographic and mathematical execution is supported by hardware-accelerated instructions including AES, SHA_NI, and AVX, though AVX-512 is absent. Software compilation with Clang and ray tracing workloads also perform in the top 25% tier. Memory performance, including read and write bandwidth, falls within the average range, as does static web serving throughput and Redis SET operations.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ccx63 offers high resource density and predictable compute performance without the risk of noisy-neighbor resource contention. This makes it highly cost-efficient for sustained, CPU-intensive workloads. The server is well-suited for software compilation, database operations, multi-threaded data decompression, and medium-scale LLM text generation.
